texts.facts: He has not committed any ofence as mentioned in the First Information Report. He is a young boy aged 26 years with no criminal antecedents. He is unmarried and residing with his parents. He is a reputed businessman. Out of political rivalry and business dispute, the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case. Pan Masala, weapons etc. was efected . As per the narration of incident given in the First Information Report, the applicant has run away from the premises as soon as he noticed Police. Still it is mentioned in the FIR that the alleged articles were seized in presence of the applicant. Besides the cash amount, Pan Masala, scented tobacco worth Rs.38,252/- was found in the house of applicant - accused no.1.

By referring the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of A Ramdhani Chaurasia & another v. State of Maharashtra & others reported at 2019 SCC OnLine Bom 1857, the learned counsel submits that mere storage of alleged contraband articles cannot even be construed as an attempt to commit ofence u/s 328 of the Indian Penal Code. In this context, the learned counsel has invited attention to paragraph nos.32 and 33 of the said decision, which read as under:- "32. The term 'causes' thus demand some action - some involvement and when we refer this term in Section 328, the upshot is that Section 328 of the IPC gets attracted in two possibilities one of administration of anything with an intent to cause hurt or indirect causation of a thing to be taken by any person with an intent to cause hurt. Mere storage without any further action and on a contemplation that it would be sold in the market, brought by a person from the market and consumed by him is too far fetched consequence of an act of 'administering' or 'causing to be taken'. By referring the allegations made in the First Information Report and the seizure of articles made from the premises, the learned APP submits that it spell out that the applicant was running the gambling den at his house.
